title: WTF Is the Context Layer? The Missing Infrastructure for Production Agents — Prukalpa Sankar
talk_summary: The speaker argues that agent performance is limited less by model intelligence than by missing business context, and describes Atlan's shift from isolated agents to a shared context layer. She proposes managing skills and context like code: versioned, owned, dependency-managed, trace-improved, portable across agent stacks, and governed for security.

takeaways.what_they_do: They centralize domain skills and business context into a common repo/company brain that multiple general-purpose agents retrieve from, instead of hardcoding context into each agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: context kind of needs to be managed like code
takeaways.numbers: about 300 skills and 40 agents in one team

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat skills as evolving artifacts that feed downstream skills, so they need dependency management, maintainers, approvers, and quality ownership.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every time they learn and evolve, it breaks something downstream

takeaways.what_they_do: They use a harness that reads agent traces, reverse-constructs what context was missing or wrong, and feeds proposed improvements back to maintainers for approve/reject.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI that's reading through all your traces and almost brings it back to your maintainer loop

takeaways.technique: Consolidate per-agent memory into shared memory
takeaways.what_they_do: They found isolated agents each learning in their own memory system created context sprawl and no single version of truth.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they were all learning separately and they were learning differently

takeaways.what_they_do: They keep context outside the agent runtime so switching from no-code builders to ADK, Glean, Claude Code, or Codex does not trap context in one system.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our context got trapped in each of these individual systems

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat context and skills as code with security posture: no hardcoded secrets, no unreviewed public skill repos, and clear governance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we had secrets hardcoded in .env files
